worked.problem: An open-top rectangular box has length 6 cm, width 4 cm, height 5 cm. A learner includes a top face. Find the first error and the required material area.
actions: Identify the base 6 cm × 4 cm; the top is open.
A closed prism has two bases, but this net has only one.
First error: the learner added a top face that does not exist.
Material area = 24 + 2(30) + 2(20) = 124 cm².
Check one base and four sides, no top; units are cm².
worked.answer: first error: included a top; material area = 124 cm²
worked.check: Check one base and four sides, no top; units are cm².
worked.misconception: Distinguish length, square and cubic units; count each face once, then verify the given radius, height and conversion.

worked.problem: A triangular prism has a right-triangle end with legs 9 cm and 12 cm, and length 6 cm. A learner omits ½. Find the first error and correct volume.
actions: Triangle legs are 9 cm and 12 cm.
The learner used the area of a rectangle, omitting the half.
First error: triangle area is ½ × 9 × 12 = 54 cm².
Volume = 54 × 6 = 324 cm³.
Check: half the enclosing rectangle gives the triangular cross-section.
worked.answer: first error: omitted ½; volume = 324 cm³
worked.check: Check: half the enclosing rectangle gives the triangular cross-section.
worked.misconception: Distinguish length, square and cubic units; count each face once, then verify the given radius, height and conversion.

worked.problem: A closed cylinder has diameter 10 cm and height 7 cm. A learner squares the diameter as the radius. Find the first error and correct volume in terms of π.
actions: The given 10 cm is a diameter.
Radius = diameter ÷ 2 = 5 cm.
First error: squaring 10 instead of the radius 5.
Volume = π × 5² × 7 = 175π cm³.
Check: using the diameter would produce four times the correct volume.
worked.answer: first error: used diameter; volume = 175π cm³
worked.check: Check: using the diameter would produce four times the correct volume.
worked.misconception: Distinguish length, square and cubic units; count each face once, then verify the given radius, height and conversion.

worked.problem: A rectangular prism has dimensions 9 cm × 3 cm × 8 cm. A learner doubles its volume when all dimensions double. Find the first error and new volume.
actions: Original volume = 9 × 3 × 8 = 216 cm³.
New dimensions are 18, 6, 16 cm.
First error: doubling all three dimensions multiplies volume by 8, not 2.
New volume = 18 × 6 × 16 = 1728 cm³.
worked.answer: first error: used factor 2; new volume = 1728 cm³
worked.misconception: Distinguish length, square and cubic units; count each face once, then verify the given radius, height and conversion.
